additional_info.subject: ID0407373-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP / P3 170000347] AC Charging port is not fully charged vehicles CRM:00641001143
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr.Ferdinand,
Hope you are doing well.
We suggest planning a site intervention to determine whether the issue is caused by the contactor or another factor, as this error can only be addressed if it occurs during a charging session. During our analysis, we observed that the contactor error has occurred multiple times.
Steps for Checking the Contactor and Its Feedback
1. Safety Precautions
Ensure the charger is powered off and locked out before performing any physical checks.
Wear appropriate PPE (insulated gloves, safety goggles, etc.).
Verify that no voltage is present before handling electrical components.
2. Visual Inspection
Check for any physical damage, burn marks, or loose wiring on the contactor.
Inspect the wiring terminals and ensure all connections are tight and secure.
Look for any signs of overheating or corrosion.
3. Check Contactor Coil Voltage
Power on the charger and start a test charging session.
Using a multimeter, measure the voltage across the coil terminals of the contactor.
If the correct voltage is present 24V DC ,the coil should energize.
If there is no voltage, check upstream control signals and relays.
4. Check Contactor Operation
Listen for a clicking sound when the contactor engages.
If there is no sound, check the coil resistance with a multimeter to see if the coil is faulty.
Manually press the contactor (if applicable) to see if it moves freely.
5. Verify Contactor Feedback Signals
Check the feedback from the auxiliary contacts (normally open or normally closed).
Use a multimeter to measure continuity across the feedback terminals:
When the contactor is energized, the normally open (NO) contact should close
7. Replacement (If Required)
If the contactor is faulty (e.g., coil not energizing, excessive resistance, or stuck contacts), replace it with a new one.
Ensure all connections are properly secured after replacement.
contactor Spare part -: 3RT2326-1BB40
Please carry a spare contactor in case a replacement is needed.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -

additional_info.subject: Note from RC
additional_info.body:
According to customer, issue was even present after
ID0374955
, but did not communicate it back.
Based off the logs attached, it appears that the charging session starts but is sometimes unable to close the contactor. There are also successful charging sessions, so it is an intermittent problem.
It also appears as if we are getting a C → B at the end, so might be worth understanding if this is with a specific vehicle, as C2 → B2 is usually the switch inside the EV saying to stop.
Could it also be that the cable is not being plugged in in the correct order, e.g. that the AC cable needs to be disconnected prior rechecking.
Order and send YHI the following spare parts:
Order Code: 3RT2326-1BB40 / Material Code: 8EM5903-0AA00-7AA7
Order Code: 3RT2926-1BB00 / Material Code: 8EM5903-0AA02-7AA8
If this does not resolve, then it is potentially an issue with the digital control.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0407373-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP / P3 170000347] AC Charging port is not fully charged vehicles CRM:00641001142
additional_info.body:
Hey Liz,
Hope you are doing well.
Regarding this case, I have reviewed the logs in a bit more detail and see 2 topics at hand here.
Sometimes the AC session is stopping and it appears someone is trying to plug it back in/restart it immediately. This would indicate to me that something is not going to plan in terms of the charging session and it might be stopping earlier than intended.
From the charger side, we are seeing a C2→B2 state change on the CP line, this C2 → B2 is usually performed by the vehicle as it opens it internal CP switch. It does not show as the contactor suddenly opening, but maybe the vehicle is seeing something that we do not have logs for.
Are you able to check with the customer if this is happening only with one specific type of vehicle? Make and model?
While not all the time, but sometimes, there does appear to be an AC contactor fault, whereby the contactor is not changing as it is intending.
It has been requested to close, but sometimes does not close. They then appear to unplug the charging cable, plug it back in and it charges the next time.
As the contactor for the AC is still operating, the cause might be the signal feeding or being received from the contactor to the controller.
Can I suggest that we update the firmware to 6.0.3 first on this charger as a proactive step and then allow the customer to provide us feedback if it is still occurring?
While there is no direct mention of this error/bug fix in the release notes and the SECC is not yet updated, this newer version also provides more logging information, which may allow us to better understand this issue at hand.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility
